statement: The system shall ingest raw telemetry from the spacecraft.
The system shall decode and validate the ingested telemetry.
The system shall convert validated telemetry into calibrated science-ready products from the particle and field instruments.
The system shall generate the operational and summary products needed by the team.
The system shall provide a recent subset of data in a form suitable for public viewing.
The facility shall package validated data products with the needed metadata and provenance.
The facility shall deliver approved products to the long-term archive.
The facility shall retain local copies as needed for traceability and reprocessing.
The system shall track processing status for received, processed, and archived data.
The ASPERA-3 science team shall have timely access to processed products for analysis, validation, and mission operations support.
Ground operations or data management staff shall ingest telemetry.
Ground operations or data management staff shall keep the pipeline running reliably.
The public or outreach audience shall access information through a simple view that is easy to access and does not expose internal data products.
The long-term archive or data center shall receive validated products in the right format for preservation and future scientific use.
The turnaround for processed products should support routine daily operations rather than batch processing over long delays.
The delivery interface should support reliable automated delivery and confirmation of receipt.
The system must provide traceability that the final approved data actually made it into the archive intact.
The system shall support separate service tiers for normal science products, public-facing summaries, and final validated deliveries.
During higher-priority mission periods or anomaly investigations, the system shall apply tighter turnaround expectations and priority handling to affected data streams.
The system shall trigger reprocessing when a calibration update is discovered.
The system shall queue reprocessing jobs behind urgent operational products.
Exact retention durations have not been fixed yet and must be agreed with the science team and archive policy.
Validated products, their reprocessed versions, and the provenance needed to reproduce them should be retained locally until they are successfully delivered and confirmed in the long-term archive.
The system should keep the final validated version plus enough metadata to trace what was produced and when.
Products with outstanding quality issues, unresolved deliveries, or a pending reprocessing campaign should be protected from purge until the issue is closed.
The ground data system shall acquire ASPERA-3 telemetry.
The ground data system shall process ASPERA-3 telemetry into science-ready products.
The ground data system shall distribute science-ready products to the team.
The ground data system shall show recent public information.
The ground data system shall preserve validated data for long-term archiving.
The facility shall support the mission instruments' data processing needs.
The telemetry processing flow is currently manual and spread across a few separate tools and scripts.
The process should keep steps consistent.
The system should ensure preserved products are tracked cleanly over the long term.
The system shall automate and standardize as much of the ingest and processing chain as possible.
The system shall make the data flow much more traceable.
The system shall provide good monitoring and reporting.
The system shall allow operators to quickly see whether a processing run failed.
The system shall provide consistent metadata handling across all products.
The system shall turn raw spacecraft telemetry into reliable science-ready data products.
The science-ready data products shall enable the ASPERA-3 team to study the particle and field environment around Mars.
The processing effort shall preserve the full mission record.
The processing effort shall make recent results available quickly enough for day-to-day mission and science use.
The validated products shall be suitable for long-term archiving.
The ground system should support publication-quality analysis.
The science team shall have access to the data continuously throughout the mission.
The system shall support checking recent data.
The system shall support revisiting older events as new questions arise.
The operational side shall be dependable and available most of the time.
The ground system shall support telemetry from the ASPERA-3 particle instruments and field instruments.
The ground system shall support related spacecraft housekeeping data needed to interpret and calibrate ASPERA-3 measurements.
The ground system shall handle instrument science packets and supporting ancillary data needed for processing.
The system shall use mission and instrument names consistently.
Product names shall make it clear whether a product is raw, processed, validated, or archive-ready.
The system shall accept partial data if that is all that arrives.
If late data arrives later, the system shall incorporate it and regenerate the affected products rather than treating the first version as final.
The system shall handle normal daily throughput comfortably.
The system shall stop and not publish a product when the input data are so incomplete or corrupted that the result would be scientifically misleading.
The workflow shall not push data downstream immediately without checks.
The workflow shall perform basic completeness checks before turning data into an analysis-ready product.
The workflow shall perform integrity checks before turning data into an analysis-ready product.
The workflow shall perform consistency checks before turning data into an analysis-ready product.
If data fall below a minimum threshold, the workflow shall hold the data or mark it as incomplete.
The minimum threshold shall be defined per processing step.
Requirement thresholds for checks before product creation shall vary by product level and by what science users need from the product.
For basic products, the system may tolerate some missing telemetry if the packet structure is intact and the gaps are clearly identified.
For analysis-ready products, the system shall require the key measurements to be present.
For analysis-ready products, the system shall require time tags to be present.
For analysis-ready products, the system shall require calibration context to be consistent enough that the results are scientifically usable.

If a processing step depends on a housekeeping stream, an attitude file, or a calibration table and that dependency is missing or obviously out of sync, the workflow shall hold or flag the output as incomplete rather than continue quietly.
If a failure appears to be a transient ingestion or transfer problem, the system shall automatically retry a few times.
If a transient ingestion or transfer problem still fails after a few automatic retries, the system shall hold the workflow.
Operator intervention is required when a failure is persistent.
Operator intervention is required when a failure affects the integrity of the product.
Operator intervention is required when a failure indicates a missing external dependency that the system cannot recover from on its own.
If a failure cannot be resolved automatically, the system shall raise a clear alert to the operations team.
The alert to the operations team shall include enough context to show what failed.
The alert to the operations team shall include enough context to show what data are affected.
The alert to the operations team shall include enough context to show whether anything was already partially processed.
The project’s own data system should be the main channel for receiving processed products.
The project’s own data system should be the controlled place the science team trusts for validated products and reprocessing history.
A shared workspace should be available for working copies.
A shared workspace should be available for quick-look items.
A shared workspace should be available for internal review.
A shared workspace should not be the primary archive path.
Direct file delivery should be supported as a convenience for specific users or transfers.
The authoritative distribution should remain centered on the project data system.
The system may support scripted or programmatic access for advanced users.
The system shall have controls around authentication.
The system shall have controls around file format.
The mission systems and the portal shall use secure transfer methods.
Archive delivery shall follow the format and packaging rules required by the archive provider.
The archive destination is usually the most constrained destination.
Protocol names and timing limits are not yet known.
Protocol names and timing limits should be defined by the interfaces already required for support rather than left open-ended.
The system shall support data integrity as a main business reason for the transfer and archive constraints.
The system shall support traceability as a main business reason for the transfer and archive constraints.
The system shall ensure that products can be accepted and preserved by the archive without rework.
The system shall apply the strictest operational limits at the archive delivery point.
The archive delivery point shall dictate the required packaging.
The archive delivery point shall dictate the required metadata.
The archive delivery point shall dictate the required validation rules.
The portal and internal mission interfaces may be more flexible than the archive delivery point if they remain secure and consistent.
The mission systems shall be reliable.
The system should assume a mixed environment unless stated otherwise.
The portal may be hosted wherever it is easiest to support secure access and availability.
There is no known hard business rule that forbids cloud use.
The publicly viewable information shall be a limited, curated subset rather than raw telemetry.
The publicly viewable information shall include recent status summaries.
The exact redaction rules for the public subset shall be defined with the science and operations teams.
The system shall treat accessibility as a serious requirement.
The granularity of telemetry and science data should follow the operational and scientific use case.
Science data can be grouped into products or bundles to make analysis and archiving easier.
Users who already received an older product should be notified if the update is significant enough to affect analysis.
The notification policy should be tied to the product type and the materiality of the change.
Users should be notified when regeneration changes the actual science content.
Purely operational changes such as reformatting or internal processing cleanup that do not affect the results should be treated as informational only and probably not warrant a direct notice.
Regenerated products shall be available as a new version rather than silently replacing the earlier version.
For active project team users, the new regenerated product version shall be pushed or prominently flagged.
The handling of regenerated products may vary by product type.

The system shall use whether people are expected to be using the product right now for current work or whether it is already part of the preserved record as the main dividing line for handling product type changes.
The way a regenerated product is pushed or flagged may differ by user group.
The project team shall receive an immediate alert for a regenerated product when required.
Versioning for a regenerated product shall stay consistent.
Notification and delivery urgency for a regenerated product may be tailored to the audience.
The archive naming should clearly reflect the mission.
The archive hierarchy and filenames should be consistent and human-readable.
The validated delivery should stand out from working or preliminary products in the Mars Express holdings.
A user should be able to identify the dataset and its maturity level without opening the files.
The system shall signal special cases very explicitly in versioning and status labels.
The current preserved record shall be marked as the active validated version.
Reprocessed or corrected deliveries shall carry clear revision identifiers and a status indicating that they supersede an earlier package.
If multiple versions are retained, the folder structure shall make the chronological order and authority order obvious so users can tell which version they should trust.
The archive delivery and preservation functions shall be hosted in a controlled environment with strong integrity and retention protections.
The public portal may be hosted more flexibly, provided that it only exposes approved recent information.
The operational processing side shall stay close to the controlled mission data flow to protect incoming telemetry and keep the chain of custody clear.
Persistent identifiers should remain stable for the same science product lineage.
Users and archives should be able to trace a science product over time.
A new identifier or catalog entry should be assigned only when the content is a different product family or a distinct deliverable.
The catalog should preserve the relationship between superseded and current versions so the history is unambiguous.
The archive shall still record whatever valid data exists.
The package shall explicitly indicate that the delivery is partial or substituted.
When streams are combined, the archive shall preserve provenance information showing which sensor sources contributed and which ones were absent.
The archive should support the ASPERA-3 particle and field instrument products that are actually being received.
The sensor taxonomy should not be hard-coded if it might later prove to be incorrect.
The system shall preserve original packet-level telemetry whenever that is what arrives.
The system shall build science bundles as derived products for analysis and distribution.
The system shall support detailed reprocessing and easier scientific use.
The archive shall recognize the ASPERA-3 instrument products that are known to be in scope.
Provisional products shall be clearly labeled as unvalidated or tentative.
The archive shall support access controls for proprietary items or embargoed items.
The archive shall support delayed release for proprietary items or embargoed items.
The existence of any special restrictions must be verified against the current agreements.
The interface shall use a secure transfer method required by the partner archive that is operationally supportable by the system.
Transfer timing shall normally follow the agreed delivery schedule.
The interface shall expedite a transfer only when there is an agreed operational need or a release deadline accepted by both sides.
The public page shall not show a placeholder that makes the page look broken or empty.
For the public subset, the published information shall be stable and clearly interpreted.
The ownership and detailed redaction rules shall be recorded as undecided for the moment.
The exact redaction rule set shall be confirmed with the science and operations teams before it is frozen.
The release notification shall be sent to operational support systems that need to react to the update.
The release notification may include a machine-readable feed for automatic consumption by another system.
Archived users should generally see the revised version with version history available.
The system shall support both a continuously available subscription channel and a pollable endpoint for the machine-readable feed, if possible.
The system's failure-handling decision should depend first on the type of failure and then on whether the failure affects data integrity or only delays processing.
The archive must be accessible for long-term preservation.
Boundary conditions for the archive environment are undecided for now.
Functions that acquire raw telemetry shall be hosted in a controlled environment.
Functions that perform validation shall be hosted in a controlled environment.
Functions that sign off products shall be hosted in a controlled environment.
Functions that transfer data into the archive shall be hosted in a controlled environment.
The public-facing recent-information service shall not interfere with the controlled processing path.
Administrative access to the archive shall be tightly controlled.
Exceptions to hosting a function farther away from the controlled mission data flow are allowed.
A function may be hosted farther away from the controlled mission data flow only if it is clearly read-only or operates on already approved products.
A function hosted farther away from the controlled mission data flow must still meet integrity requirements.
A function hosted farther away from the controlled mission data flow must still meet access-control requirements.
A function that touches raw telemetry must not be moved farther away from the controlled mission data flow.
A function that touches validation state must not be moved farther away from the controlled mission data flow.
A function that touches archive ingress must not be moved farther away from the controlled mission data flow.
Borderline cases require formal review and approval before allowing separation from the controlled mission data flow.
A new identifier should be assigned only when the reprocessed item is effectively a different product line or a materially different dataset that should not be treated as a replacement.
Ingestion shall be the first and highest-priority stage.
If spacecraft data is not safely ingested, no other mission processing can proceed.
Science processing and archive delivery shall be next in line after ingestion.
Distribution to the project team shall occur as soon as trustworthy products are available.
Public access shall not take precedence over the controlled mission flow.
If there is a bottleneck, the system shall prioritize the raw data path, validation, and archive preservation before any public-facing activity.
The system shall ensure reliable delivery of the preserved products to the archive and the project team.
The system should provide public viewing of recent information as a desirable but secondary capability.
Desirable features shall be enabled only when they do not interfere with ingestion, validation, or preservation.
Desirable features shall ideally be enabled only after the operational products have been secured and handed off.
Public release features shall be deferred until the mission-facing data path is stable and the approved content is ready.
Desirable features shall be deferred if they risk slowing down archive delivery or complicating traceability.
The system shall hold a product back from long-term archive holdings if its provenance is unclear.
The system shall hold a product back from long-term archive holdings if validation has not completed.
The system shall hold a product back from long-term archive holdings if the metadata is incomplete.
The system shall hold a product back from long-term archive holdings if unresolved quality issues could mislead future users.
The system shall allow an exception only if the science team explicitly signs off that the product is still worth preserving.
The system shall require the limitation to be documented when an exception is allowed.
The system shall clearly label an exception product as provisional or nonstandard.
The system shall send a processed product forward only when the package is complete.
The system shall send a processed product forward only when the metadata is sufficient for later discovery and use.
The system shall send a processed product forward only when validation results show it is fit for archive.
Validated products shall be retained indefinitely.
Validated products shall be stored in a stable preservation format.
If a community or agency archive standard exists, the system shall align with that standard for validated products.
The system shall escalate a failure immediately if the failure affects ingestion, could cause data loss, or blocks archive delivery.
The system shall allow a short retry window before paging operations if the failure appears transient, such as a brief connectivity or downstream service glitch.
The alert context shall vary by stage.
The project data management lead shall make the activation decision in coordination with archive operations.
The system shall allow local action without escalation for routine operational responses that do not change the retention policy.
The system shall allow local reallocation of storage space.
The system shall allow local delay of noncritical staging.
The system shall allow moving products within approved storage tiers if the action stays inside existing rules.
The system shall require escalation when an action would shorten retention.
The system shall require escalation when an action would dispose of validated products.
The system shall require escalation when an action would create any policy exception.
A local action shall be escalated for project management review if it would have any irreversible impact or alter the approved preservation strategy.
A local action shall be escalated for project management review if it changes what gets kept, how long it is kept, or the scientific risk associated with it.
A workaround shall be escalated for project management review if the same workaround has to be used repeatedly.
A local storage workaround shall be brought to project management when it is repeated often enough that it consumes staff time.
A local storage workaround shall be brought to project management when it delays product delivery.
A local storage workaround shall be brought to project management when it leaves no real buffer against the next data surge.
The system shall reliably receive science telemetry generated by the ASPERA-3 instruments on Mars Express.
The system shall preserve science telemetry generated by the ASPERA-3 instruments on Mars Express for the mission team.
The system shall transform raw incoming data into usable science products.
The system shall show recent results to the public.
The system shall keep validated data safe for long-term archiving.
The system shall serve as the operational bridge between spacecraft telemetry and day-to-day scientific use and permanent mission preservation.
The system shall provide dependable end-to-end handling of data from acquisition through processing, distribution, and archival without losing or corrupting anything.
The system shall monitor processing success rates.
The system shall monitor the number of products needing reprocessing or manual correction.
The system shall prioritize completeness, turnaround time, and low error rates.
The ASPERA-3 science team shall be the primary users of the system.
Operations and data management staff shall rely on the system for reliable ingestion.
Science users shall be able to pull down products.
The system shall provide stable formats for science users.
Operations and data management personnel shall be able to watch the ingestion pipeline.
The system shall promote validated datasets into the archive correctly.
The facility shall start a typical processing run when new spacecraft telemetry arrives from the mission data source.
When telemetry is missing or late, operations staff shall investigate the gap.
Where appropriate, the facility shall make archived science products available for public viewing.
The facility shall react to processing failures.
The facility shall react to data quality anomalies.
The facility shall react to periodic operational milestones such as delivery closure or archive release.
The system shall recognize raw telemetry as a mission-data term.
The system shall distinguish nominal data from other data statuses.
Raw telemetry is the direct mission data received from the spacecraft before any science or formatting transformations are applied.
The transition between product states is driven by successful processing, review, and packaging.
Nominal data is treated as the normal case.
Gaps are recorded so users understand that the product is incomplete.
Nothing shall be promoted to validated or archive-ready until the relevant processing is complete and the science team has accepted it.
A later packet can change an interval that was already processed.
The facility shall support controlled reprocessing and replacement.
The system shall support version control for products.
The system shall define when a product is considered stable enough to be frozen for archive.
The system shall support reprocessing campaigns that affect a large time span.
The system shall support validation-related sensitivity in product workflow decisions.
The system shall support delivery windows tied to internal processing cadence and archive submission expectations.
The system shall require products to meet prescribed formats and metadata conventions.
The system shall allow public-facing release timing to be flexible.
The system shall require public-facing releases to follow project approval and any embargo or review rules before data is published.
The facility shall use an intake interface from the mission telemetry source or ground segment to receive raw spacecraft packets.
The system shall provide a short user guide.
The system shall provide a few worked examples.
The system shall make unclear information visible in the metadata instead of requiring users to guess or ask the team.
Scientists shall be able to get the right product quickly.
Scientists shall be able to understand a product's pedigree.
Operations staff shall have predictable ingest and reprocessing.
The system shall provide clear status indicators.
The system shall use stable product naming.
The system shall reduce confusion when a file gets replaced later.
The system shall remove ambiguity about whether a product is the latest accepted version.
The system shall use operational monitoring of ingest queues, job completion, and file counts to detect when data stops moving or arrives late.

If a processing step fails, the system shall alert the operations team quickly and retain enough logs to determine whether the issue was in the incoming telemetry, the transform, or the delivery path.
For data loss or delays, the system shall perform checks against expected deliveries and provide gap reporting so the team can decide whether to wait, re-run, or flag the affected products.
The facility shall scale mainly by adding processing capacity and storage rather than redesigning the whole workflow.
Mission data growth occurs in bursts when reprocessing campaigns happen.
Reliability shall be prioritized over raw speed.
Any expansion shall preserve the same validation rules.
Any expansion shall preserve the same provenance rules.
Any expansion shall preserve the same archival rules.
There is no specific upgrade plan yet.
The upgrade approach shall depend on how the load trends over time and what infrastructure the project team is allowed to use.
The system shall provide a short overview page.
Some users need human guidance the first time they work with the archive.
Feedback from the science team and occasional users shall be used informally as the main mechanism for evaluating onboarding effectiveness.
The system shall balance rapid data release against waiting until products are sufficiently validated.
The system shall replace preliminary products with final products once validation is complete.
The system shall preserve full traceability while keeping the workflow simple.
For science use, the system shall accept additional process overhead when needed to support provenance and reproducibility.
The system shall allow early release of a data set when it is needed quickly for science planning and calibration or quality checks are still underway.
The system shall use stricter versioning and better status metadata.
The archive shall retain both the earlier form and the validated form of a product without losing integrity.
